correctness.rationale: On the diagonal, q maps to 4q−3(1+α+β)q²; w=3(1+α+β)q/4 gives logistic four, a factor of Lebesgue doubling by w=sin²(πt). This proves the invariant ergodic arcsine law. The tangent log multiplier has mean log 2. Direct differentiation gives a circulant with first row (4−3(2+α+β)q,−3αq,−3βq). The fixed orthogonal real Fourier splitting gives the longitudinal multiplier 4(1−2w) and a conformal transverse block with complex multiplier 4(1−w)+Bw, up to conjugation. Each transverse product has two equal singular values. The logs are integrable, including a zero of the multiplier at an interior point or the endpoint. With v=√B/2 and ρ=(1−v)/(1+v), the transverse integral becomes 2 log|1+v| plus a full-circle average of log|1+ρe^{it}|. The latter is zero by Jensen for |ρ|<1, and for |ρ|=1 by a shift and the elementary log-sine integral; thus even negative real B and B=0 are included. The squared modulus is 1+Re√B+|B|/4, equal to one only at α=β=1. On α+β=2 the real root part is √(|α−β|/√3) and the |B|/4 term has order |α−β|, giving the claimed cusp constant. This is a pointwise a.e. ambient spectrum under the specified singular diagonal probability, not an assertion about a physical basin.
residual_risks: No claim about exceptional diagonal orbits, non-diagonal invariant measures, or R other than 3.

value.rationale: The exact two-coupling spectrum settles a meaningful stability question on the whole positive quadrant: under the canonical chaotic diagonal probability there is no infinitesimal transverse attraction, and precisely one neutral point. Holding total competition fixed isolates the effect of asymmetry and gives an explicit nonanalytic response coefficient that the symmetric slice cannot predict. These are usable exact benchmarks for dynamical studies near neutrality, not merely a restatement of the symmetric law or a fit to numerical charts.
residual_risks: Scientific value is for the invariant-measure cocycle and its local stability interpretation, not a global attractor classification.
